name: Tamar
whenBasis: In David's reign, ≈1010–970 BC, counted back from Solomon as Thiele and most chronologies do.
summary: David's beautiful daughter, full sister of Absalom. Sent by the king to make food for Amnon, who pretended to be ill, she was raped by him and then thrown out. She put ashes on her head, tore the robe worn by the king's virgin daughters, and went away crying aloud. She lived desolate in Absalom's house.
body: She is the one who speaks reason in the room: she pleads with Amnon not to do this disgraceful thing, asks what would become of her shame and of him, and tells him to speak to the king. Sent away, she says that sending her away is worse than the great wrong he has already done.
Absalom tells her to keep quiet, for he is her brother, and names his own daughter Tamar.
